subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Writing to argue and persuade; end of year
source: Written for english/y8 lesson 80 (Pupil's marked Section B and feedback (portal))
intro: Lesson 80: Test feedback: writing DIRT. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Teacher-written model response for TGA
paras: The city did not notice me. Buses sighed at the kerb, their windows full of tired faces turned away; a food stall hissed and spat, sending up clouds of cumin and smoke; somewhere above, a train rattled across a bridge like a zip being pulled. I stood still, holding my suitcase, and the street flowed round me as if I were a stone in a river.

keywords.def: ideas, structure and fit to purpose
a list of your common mistakes and their fixes

questions.q: Add your three most common errors to your error log with a fix
Core: redraft one paragraph of your Section B answer using your feedback and the model
Extend: proofread the whole piece and fix every logged error
Stretch: rewrite your ending so it echoes your opening
Which redraft best improves 'The street was busy and loud.'?
options: The street was busy, loud and big.
Buses sighed at the kerb and a stall hissed and spat.
The street was very, very busy.
questions.a: B) Buses sighed at the kerb and a stall hissed and spat.. Precise verbs and personification show busyness instead of telling it.
